correctness.rationale: A nonzero idempotent is equivalent to precisely one fixed point of the projectivized squaring-composed invertible map. The fixed-point determinant is a nonzero homogeneous cubic, so \(0\le N\le3\). PGL2 acts sharply transitively on ordered triples of distinct directions. The projective squaring map has no collisions for even q and exactly \(q-1\) ordered pair collisions for odd q. Counting ordered 1-,2-,3-tuples yields factorial moments, with odd-characteristic \(T_2=q^2+1\) and \(T_3=(q-1)(q^2-2q+3)\); inversion proves all four exact probabilities including \(\Pr[N=0]=1/3\). Full exhaustions over \(q\in\{2,3,4,5,7,8,9\}\) and independently raw vector enumeration for \(q\in\{2,3,5,7\}\) match; computations test cases, not infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The primary 2026 survey (Theorem 18, Remark 23, Conjecture 2) gives existence, expected count one and an asymptotic symmetric-group model, but no exact four-value finite-q law. Prior isomorphism-class formulas are for a distinct sampling measure. The known second moment does not imply the four-value distribution since the third factorial moment is independent: this theorem calculates it from a new exact ordered-triple projective collision count. Actual literature, mathematical-record, and alias searches found no dominating complete distribution. A general preexisting projective-map statistics theorem could nevertheless imply it, and full historical priority remains unconfirmed.

value.rationale: The four-value distribution is the complete probabilistic invariant for the first nontrivial dimension of the uniform perfect evolution-algebra model. The exact universal \(1/3\) probability of idempotent-free algebras quantitatively sharpens mere existence, and even characteristic has the exact \(S_3\) fixed-point law for every q whereas odd characteristic has a nonzero, explicit correction of size \((q-1)/(q(q+1))\). The projective squaring collision mechanism explains the dichotomy and gives a benchmark for the 2026 survey’s finite-field asymptotic prediction. Results concern a natural entire family, not an arbitrary isolated computation.
